और कभी-कभी हम एक स्थान से दूसरे स्थान को उड़ते विमान भी देखते हैं। इस प्रकार यह दृश्य

शक्ति की सृष्टि के अन्तर्गत प्रकट हुए हैं, जो एक ही समय उनसे अभिन्न है तथा भिन्न भी हैं; अतः

The Gods said: We bow to that divine form of God who created this world
in the form of his external power, which is situated in them in the same way as air
and clouds live in the sky, and who has now appeared in the house of Dharma as Nar-Narayan Rishi. Meaning: The immense form of God is this visible world, which is a display of the external power of Shri Bhagavan.
In the sky, there are countless diverse types of worlds, and there is also air; in the air, there are colorful clouds.
And sometimes we see airplanes flying from one place to another. Thus, this scene
The world is full of diversity, but in reality, this diversity is a display of God's outward power
And this power is located in them. After manifesting his power, now God himself has manifested within the creation of his own
power, who is one at the same time, is inseparable from him, and is also different; therefore,
the gods bowed to Shri Bhagavan, who manifested in many forms. Some atheistic philosophers
believe these forms to be false because of their formless thought. In this verse, it is specifically said--Yo Mayaya Virachitam / This indicates that these forms are manifestations of the power of Shri Bhagavan.
(Sarupya). Thus, because of their being inseparable from the Lord of Shakti, these forms are real. Physical
Forms may be momentary, but they are not false. They are reflections of the self.
Here, the word used for 'pratichakshanaya'
means 'they are forms (of what)' declaring the glory of Shri Bhagavan, who has manifested in the form of Nar-Narayan,
and who is the root of all forms of material nature. He who is situated, who removes the obstacles, the creator,
He is not to be compared to the gods by his truthfulness, that essence.

Those who, through the study of material knowledge and logic, have become inert like matter, they
are engaged in infinite desires and actions. Such humans have deliberately disrespected Lord Shiva. Such people remain trapped in the cycle of birth and death.

Meaning: The three curses described here are sufficient to make anyone as inert as stone, devoid of self-knowledge,
and to keep them engaged in material knowledge. After giving these curses, Nandishwar
cursed the Brahmins that they remain in the cycle of birth and death, because they have supported Daksha in disrespecting Shivji.
